answer: Each agent carries a signed cold-chain log of every interaction, so a fabricated identity leaves a discontinuous plume of missing custody stamps that verifiers flag before any transaction settles. Registries cross-check these logs against a jade ledger of countersigned handoffs, making each new sybil cost a full forged history rather than a cheap keypair. The sable limit: colluding agents that faithfully cosign each other's fabricated chain can still pass, so resistance scales with the cost of sustaining plausible custody, not with identity count alone.
